text.p: Merrill Lynch, in its latest research report on SKB, recommends investors reduce their holdings in Slovenia's second largest bank after it reported disappointing first half results.
"Earnings dropped 17 percent as provisions jumped and the bank's margins suffered from adverse currency movements," Merrill Lynch said in the report, dated August 12.
Merrill Lynch said it had downgraded its recommendation on the shares for the medium-term to "reduce" from "neutral".

"With uncertainty remaining over the central bank's currency policy in Slovenia we consider the risk reward of owning this stock unwarranted in the intermediate term, and recommend investors to reduce their holdings," it said.
At the very least margins are set to remain under pressure in the second half of this year, it said.
Last week SKB reported a drop in pre-tax profit for the first six month to 1.5 billion tolars from 1.8 billion in the same period of the last year. No net figures were given at the interim period.
SKB shares closed 1.41 percent lower at 2,650 tolars on volume of 1,995 shares. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
